name: The Coca-Cola Company

segments.note: Segment revenue includes sales between segments. Bottling Investments (revenue $5.7B, operating income $400M) not shown. Corporate costs were $1.8B ($5.3B in 2024, which included fairlife-related charges).

footnotes: Operating cash flow and free cash flow are reduced by a contingent payment of about $6.1B for the fairlife acquisition; Coca-Cola reported free cash flow of $11.4B excluding it. Equity income & other, net = $2.0B equity income + $1.1B other income + $800M interest income − $1.7B interest expense.

Bottling, corp. & elims. = Bottling Investments + Corporate revenue − eliminations between segments, so the flow chart adds to total revenue. Total debt = loans and notes payable + current maturities + long-term debt.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Coca-Cola's net operating revenues grew 1.9% to $47.9B in 2025, with flat unit case volume. North America grew 3.8% and EMEA 5.1%. Operating income jumped 37.7% to $13.8B, mainly because 2024 included large fairlife-related charges.
Net income rose 23.3% to $13.1B, or $3.04 per share. A one-time fairlife payment held free cash flow to $5.3B; excluding it, free cash flow was $11.4B. Dividends rose 5.0% to $8.8B.
highlights: North America operating income rose 11.3% to $5.1B.
2026 outlook calls for 4%–5% organic revenue growth.
watch: Free cash flow was cut by the fairlife payment.
sources: Coca-Cola Q4 and full-year 2025 results (SEC exhibit)
